If the fetch API response is returned directly from the handler, c.res contains the raw fetch API response. In that case, even if c.res.clone() is done, the header is still immutable, so I think this would result in the same error as the following issue.

https://github.com/honojs/hono/issues/3316



```
> const req = (await fetch('https://hono.dev/')).clone()
> req.headers.set('Hono-Cache-Expiration', '1')
Uncaught TypeError: immutable
```
https://github.com/honojs/hono/pull/3318 will solve the issue, right?

Thanks for confirming.
I guess #3318 doesn't solve the problem.

If you run the following app with deno, you will see that `TypeError: Headers are immutable.`

```ts
import { Hono } from './src/hono'
import { cache } from './src/middleware/cache'

const app = new Hono()
app.use(cache({
  cacheName: Math.random().toString(),
  cacheControl: 'max-age=3600',
  wait: true,
  duration: 100,
}))
app.get('/', (c) => fetch('https://hono.dev/'))

export default app
```

```
TypeError: Headers are immutable.
    at Headers.set (ext:deno_fetch/20_headers.js:425:13)
    at cache (file:///Users/taku/src/github.com/honojs/hono/src/middleware/cache/index.ts:135:19)
    at eventLoopTick (ext:core/01_core.js:168:7)
    at async dispatch (file:///Users/taku/src/github.com/honojs/hono/src/compose.ts:74:17)
    at async file:///Users/taku/src/github.com/honojs/hono/src/hono-base.ts:444:25
    at async ext:deno_http/00_serve.ts:364:18
```

This is a very redundant cloning process, but to avoid this, the following should be done.

```diff
diff --git a/src/middleware/cache/index.ts b/src/middleware/cache/index.ts
index 6c04207d..6d122589 100644
--- a/src/middleware/cache/index.ts
+++ b/src/middleware/cache/index.ts
@@ -130,7 +132,10 @@ export const cache = (options: {
       return
     }
     addHeader(c)
-    const res = c.res.clone()
+    const res = new Response(c.res.clone().body, {
+      status: c.res.status,
+      headers: c.res.headers,
+    })
     if (options.duration) {
       res.headers.set(cachedTime, String(Date.now()))
     }
```

Alternatively, if one were to avoid this overhead in the normal case, this might be a good approach.

```diff
diff --git a/src/middleware/cache/index.ts b/src/middleware/cache/index.ts
index 6c04207d..0be76724 100644
--- a/src/middleware/cache/index.ts
+++ b/src/middleware/cache/index.ts
@@ -130,9 +132,22 @@ export const cache = (options: {
       return
     }
     addHeader(c)
-    const res = c.res.clone()
+    let res = c.res.clone()
     if (options.duration) {
-      res.headers.set(cachedTime, String(Date.now()))
+      try {
+        res.headers.set(cachedTime, String(Date.now()))
+      } catch (e) {
+        if (e instanceof TypeError && e.message.includes('immutable')) {
+          // `res` is immutable (probably a response from a fetch API), so retry with a new response.
+          res = new Response(res.body, {
+            headers: res.headers,
+            status: res.status,
+          })
+          res.headers.set(cachedTime, String(Date.now()))
+        } else {
+          throw e
+        }
+      }
     }
     if (options.wait) {
       await cache.put(key, res)
```

It may be possible to provide a utility method, but that is up to preference.

According to https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7234#section-5.2 it is case insensitive, so it is better to add `i`.

```suggestion
const cacheControlNoTransformRegExp = /(?:^|,)\s*?no-transform\s*?(?:,|$)/i
```

If `max-age=20` is `Max-age=20`, the test will fail. If it compares the names of the directives, I think we have to make all uppercase letters lowercase first.

If there is a cost to lowercase, you might prefer to lowercase everything first, even if only `directives`.
